headline: The Real Reason OnePlus Failed in the US
reasoning: This topic scores highly due to its strong clickability within the tech enthusiast community and its relevance to the broader consumer market. The failure of a major phone brand is significant news, and the underlying reason—the economics of the US carrier system—is a relatable and practical issue for anyone who buys a smartphone. The story also lends itself to multiple engaging formats, from a 'hot take' on the US phone market to a practical listicle of alternative devices.
summary: OnePlus has officially ceased operations in the United States after struggling to gain a foothold. The brand's failure is attributed to its value-focused, 'flagship killer' model being fundamentally incompatible with the US market's reliance on carrier financing for expensive phones.

source_articles.title: OnePlus never had a chance in the US
source_articles.excerpt: Twelve years after the launch of the OnePlus One, OnePlus announced today that it has exited the United States. It's bittersweet, as the brand has been on a comeback tour of sorts with its excellent OnePlus 15 and widely praised (though still too expensive) OnePlus Open.
